concept.title: About Merge and Rebase
concept.shortdesc: Merge and rebase both combine two lines of work, but they keep the history differently.

conbody.p: When your branch and the branch you are integrating have both moved on, Git has to reconcile them. You have two strategies to choose from:

dlentry.dd: Joins the two histories with a merge commit. Your existing commits stay exactly as they were, and the merge commit records that the two lines came together. History is complete but not linear.

Replays your local commits on top of the other branch, one by one, so the history stays linear, as if you had started your work from the latest state. Because it rewrites your commits, use it only on commits you have not shared yet.

conbody.p: Either strategy can produce conflicts, which you resolve the same way. See .
